claims.statement: Control-plane state is split by consistency role: per-session Durable Object SQLite (ctx.storage.sql) is the authoritative store for a single session's behavioural state, D1 (env.DB) is the shared queryable index/registry (session listings, environments, secrets, automations, image builds, users, provider accounts), R2 (env.MEDIA_BUCKET) holds opaque media bytes, and KV (env.REPOS_CACHE) holds caches that may be discarded at any time.

The Session Durable Object's SQLite schema (src/session/schema.ts) owns session, participants, messages, events, artifacts, attachments, sandbox, session_repositories, session_diff, session_alarm_state and ws_client_mapping, plus unique indexes that encode invariants such as at most one processing message per session.

Git working state lives only in the session Durable Object: the DO's session_repositories table carries branch_name/base_sha/current_sha, while D1's session_repositories stores the identity subset (owner, name, repo_id, base_branch) because D1 does not store git state.

Every src/db D1 store takes the engine-neutral SqlDatabase port (prepare/batch) in its constructor; D1Database satisfies it structurally with a compile-time assignability assertion, and the port is explicitly a different thing from the Durable Object's synchronous SqlStorage.

SqlResultMeta.changes is a required field the stores gate correctness on (CAS conflict detection, guarded lifecycle transitions, insert/upsert detection across roughly 38 call sites), while duration/rows_read/rows_written are observability-only and must never be used to decide correctness.

SqlDatabase.batch() is contractually one atomic transaction with a single consistent snapshot and positional 1:1 results; stores rely on this for delete-then-insert replacements and multi-query reads, and an adapter may not emulate it with independent round-trips.

Reading env.DB is banned by an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule across packages/control-plane/src; the only legitimate reads are composition roots (router.ts request handle, index.ts entrypoints, the finalization Queue consumer, and the SessionDO constructor), each carrying an inline disable with justification.

instrumentD1(db, metrics) wraps a SqlDatabase by object composition so every first/run/all records wall-clock time and engine meta into a per-request RequestMetrics accumulator, letting stores be timed without any store change; the summary is spread into the http.request wide event by ctx.metrics.summarize().

Instrumented statements carry the underlying statement under the ORIGINAL_STMT symbol and are unwrapped before db.batch(), because the engine can only execute its own prepared statements — the same-origin contract documented on the SqlDatabase port.

BackgroundTasks.submit(task, {name, context}) is the platform port for deferring work past the request; the Cloudflare implementation over ExecutionContext.waitUntil absorbs and logs both a synchronous throw from the factory and a later rejection as background_task.failed, so building a background task can never fail its caller. The Durable Object composition root builds one over its own execution context.

D1's session cost/rollup columns are derived caches over Durable Object truth: SessionStatusService reads total_cost, message count, active duration, and PR artifact count synchronously from the DO and submits sessionIndex.updateMetrics() as a background task.

Session creation is ordered D1-index-first then DO-init: SessionIndexStore.create() inserts the session row, ordered repositories, skill manifest, and provider-auth snapshot in one atomic batch and throws if the insert was skipped, so D1 failures surface before a sandbox is spawned.

When DO init fails or the transport errors, initialize.ts runs best-effort compensation by marking the D1 index row failed, so a half-created session does not linger as a phantom 'created' row in listings.
SessionIndexStore.updateStatus guards against out-of-order async projections with 'WHERE id = ? AND updated_at <= ?', so a stale projector matches no rows and returns false.

repairStatus() deliberately omits the updated_at guard used by updateStatus, because the Durable Object's own timestamp is behind D1's whenever touchUpdatedAt has run — the guarded write would match no rows and report a successful repair as false. It asserts only the stale 'created' shape and leaves updated_at meaning last real activity.

Child-session capacity is reserved in D1 before the child exists: acquireChildAdmissionLease inserts only when (active children + unexpired leases) is below the limit, with ON CONFLICT(child_session_id) refresh gated on expiry, and the lease is deleted by finalizeChildAdmission only after the child's own 'active' projection to the index succeeds.

The abandoned-draft sweep closes the index/DO divergence loop: it selects D1 rows still 'created' past an 8h TTL (oldest-first, capped at 50), asks each Durable Object to retire itself, and treats a 404 as a definitive answer so archiveOrphanedDraft() retires the index row on its own, still guarded on status = 'created'.

The DO's expire-draft route is the authority on its own state: a session no longer 'created' answers not_draft and repairs the stale index mirror, and a 'created' session that nevertheless holds messages settles from message state instead of being archived, so a broken row cannot pin the head of the oldest-first batch forever.

Environments use a deliberate cascade model: environment_repositories, environment_secrets and integration_environment_settings are ON DELETE CASCADE owned children, while image-build rows and sessions.environment_id are intentionally FK-less so deleting an entity supersedes builds (leaving the reaper able to delete provider artifacts) and leaves session provenance benignly dangling.

All three secret scopes — global_secrets, repo_secrets (keyed by repo_id), and environment_secrets — store AES-GCM ciphertext encrypted with the same REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, with shared validation plumbing (uppercase key normalization, reserved keys, size and count caps) in db/scoped-secrets.ts.
Secret writes are bounded by hard caps enforced before encryption: 16 KiB per value, 64 KiB combined per scope, 50 keys per scope, and a 128 KiB ceiling on a session's merged secret payload.

Secrets-at-rest encryption is not optional inside the Durable Object: createSessionRuntime resolves requireRepoSecretsEncryptionKey(env) and requireTokenEncryptionKey(env) before constructing any consumer, so no fallback path can persist a secret in plaintext.

Integration settings resolve through three D1 layers — integration_settings (global), integration_repo_settings (per-repo), integration_environment_settings (per-environment, the top layer restricted by the store to session-scoped integrations) — and sessions resolve them once at create time.

image_builds (migration 0039) is a single prebuilt-image registry keyed by scope_kind ('repo'|'environment') + scope_id, replacing repo_images and environment_images asymmetrically: environment rows are copied verbatim because they already carry fingerprints (preserving prebuild continuity), while repo_images rows are dropped un-migrated as cache entries, accepting slower boots until the rebuild cron regenerates them.

image_builds carries three column clusters: matching identity (repositories_fingerprint, repository_shas, runtime_version), callback authority (provider_session_id, callback_token_hash/expires_at/used_at), and Queue-finalization state added by migration 0052 (completion_hash, finalization_lease_token/expires_at, provider_session_cleanup_pending).

The repositories fingerprint is a SHA-256 over ordered, lowercased owner/name with case-sensitive branch names, computed only control-plane-side (build registration and spawn matching) so the algorithm has exactly one home; order is significant because setup hooks run in position order.

Image-build callbacks authenticate with a single-use bearer token whose only stored form is an HMAC-SHA256 hash under IMAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN_PEPPER with a frozen 'repo-image-callback:' domain-separation prefix, and every callback must also present the exact provider session id bound to the row.

The per-(scope, provider) build state machine caps live rows at one 'building' (registerBuild is an INSERT...SELECT guarded by NOT EXISTS on that predicate) plus one 'ready' (marking ready supersedes older readies), which is why cross-scope status reads can be unbounded without hiding a live build.

Long provider work is moved outside the request-lifetime durability window: the callback atomically accepts the completion in D1 (consuming the token and writing completion_hash), then a small secret-free versioned job is sent to IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_QUEUE whose consumer performs the snapshot, publishes ready/superseded, and does idempotent teardown.

The completion hash is a deterministic SHA-256 over a canonicalized callback document (lowercased repo owner/name, sorted SHAs, and a frozen millisecond buildDurationMs), stored on the build row and checked by the finalizer before any work, so stale or duplicated Queue commands are recognized and dropped rather than re-applied.

Finalization concurrency is serialized by a D1 lease: claimLease takes the row only when the lease is free or expired, recordArtifact fences the provider image id to build+provider+session+completion-hash+lease-token while provider_image_id IS NULL, and markFailed/clearLease only act while the caller still owns finalization_lease_token (6-minute lease around a 5-minute provider deadline).

The finalization consumer applies at-least-once semantics per message — unparseable jobs are acked and logged, a retry disposition retries with the computed delay, and an unexpected throw retries at 15s without aborting later messages — matching the Terraform consumer settings (batch_size 1, max_concurrency 5, max_retries 12, DLQ).

Recovery is driven by D1 state rather than queue state: the scheduler's republish phase selects building rows with a used callback token, a completion hash, and no live lease (ordered to match the partial idx_image_builds_finalization_recovery index) and re-sends a job per row, tolerating a missing queue binding.

test/integration/image-build-finalization-queue.test.ts drives the Worker queue entrypoint end-to-end over real D1 migrations to prove a build whose provider artifact was already recorded resumes without snapshotting again.

image_builds status transitions are guarded by purpose: supersedeActiveImages flips building and ready rows on a secret change, markRestoreFailed flips only ready rows from the spawn path so the rebuild cron regenerates them, and quarantineArtifact terminalizes to failed only while still building so an out-of-band supersede stays superseded.

Spawn-time image selection separates concerns: resolveScopeEnabled answers scope existence and prebuild enablement (false for a deleted scope or a disabled one), and only then ImageBuildStore.getLatestReadyForSpawn performs the plain row read — scope.ts is the only module that switches on scope kind.

image_builds never links to a session row: the spawn path matches by scope and fingerprint and carries image_build_id only in Durable Object sandbox state and logs, so the registry can be superseded without any per-session join.

An automation invocation's status is never stored: DERIVED_INVOCATION_STATUS_SQL in db/automation-store.ts is the single definition (childless = skipped; any active child = starting then running; all-terminal = completed/failed/partial_failed/skipped) and is interpolated into both listInvocations and the automation-list executions rollup.

deriveInvocationStatus() is a TypeScript twin of the SQL definition over a sibling run aggregate, and integration tests assert the two agree on every case; the twin requires a separate starting count because the aggregate folds starting and running into 'active'.

Invocation completedAt is also derived (MAX(child completed_at) once all children are terminal), with one app-level exception: a childless skip is settled at creation, so toAutomationInvocation substitutes created_at when skip_reason is set and no children exist.

Automations persist as automations (config, next_run_at, consecutive_failures) + live selections in automation_repositories and automation_environments + one thin automation_invocations row per firing (source, scheduled_at, trigger_key, concurrency_key, skip_reason, failure_counted_at) + automation_runs, one row per target per invocation, carrying a firing-time snapshot of the target.

Firing dedup is enforced by two partial unique indexes on automation_invocations — (automation_id, scheduled_at) WHERE source='schedule' for cron double-fires and (automation_id, trigger_key) WHERE trigger_key IS NOT NULL for events — while per-target uniqueness uses idx_runs_invocation_repo and idx_runs_invocation_environment on automation_runs.

insertInvocationGuarded creates the invocation, its children, and the schedule advance in one batch with every statement self-guarded, because D1 batch() rolls back only on statement error — a 0-row INSERT...SELECT is a success — and the advance is a compare-and-set on the exact slot claimed so a losing tick cannot skip a cron slot.

isDuplicateKeyError() only classifies a failure as a duplicate when the message contains 'UNIQUE constraint failed' and names trigger_key or automation_invocations, so unrelated unique violations keep surfacing as real errors; db/errors.ts holds the engine-neutral isUniqueConstraintError() as the adapter extension point.

Run state changes are single guarded SQL updates rather than read-then-write: updateRun appends AND status IN ('starting','running') so a terminal run can never transition again, claimRunSession binds a session only while status='starting', and the bulk failure sweeps carry AND status = ? so a sweep only affects rows still in the state it observed.

Auto-pause accounting is exactly-once via a compare-and-set stamp: tryMarkInvocationFailureCounted sets failure_counted_at only WHERE failure_counted_at IS NULL, so whichever racing callback wins is the only one that counts the invocation's failure.

The automation recovery sweep queries orphaned 'starting' and timed-out 'running' runs by literal status values (documented as required for the planner to use the partial sweep indexes), and the scheduler bulk-fails them; automation_runs is never joined to sessions to detect a dead session.

The run-to-session link is soft in both directions: automation_runs.session_id (partial index idx_runs_session) plus mirrored sessions.automation_id/automation_run_id columns from migration 0013, with no foreign keys, so deleting a session does not retroactively fail its run.

repo_metadata (with JSON aliases/keywords/channel associations, default_environment_id, and the image_build_enabled toggle) and the repo/user identity tables are D1-side registries: repo_metadata is the repo-scope enablement source read by the image-build scheduler, and users/user_identities link provider identities to a canonical user id used across sessions and automations.
R2 access is funneled through the four-method ObjectStorage port (put/delete/head/range-get) implemented by R2ObjectStorage over env.MEDIA_BUCKET via createMediaObjectStorage(env).

R2 keys are session-scoped by construction: sessions/<sessionId>/attachments/<attachmentId> for user attachments and sessions/<sessionId>/media/<artifactId>.<ext> for agent screenshots and recordings.

Attachment upload registers the record in the Durable Object before writing bytes to R2, so every failed or ambiguous storage outcome stays discoverable through the stale-attachment cleanup protocol; per-session file-count and byte quotas are enforced inside the single-threaded DO.

Attachment registration is a two-phase protocol (record / complete_cleanup) over the DO's internal route with a versioned zod command schema: the DO claims stale unreferenced rows and returns their object keys, the caller deletes them in R2 and acknowledges or releases each id, and a release fails the upload with cleanup_failed rather than silently exceeding quota.

The DO's attachments table is the registry for R2 objects (id, mime_type, size_bytes, object_key, message_id, cleanup_claimed_at); message_id is claimed transactionally — claimForMessage throws AttachmentClaimConflictError unless rowsWritten equals the requested id count — and unreferenced rows are swept after a TTL.

Agent media is inverted relative to attachments and validated through the DO: the artifact record is persisted into DO artifacts after the R2 put (with compensating deletion of the uploaded object when persistence fails), and reads fetch the artifact from the DO before streaming from R2, so an artifact id cannot address another session's object.

The /repos listing uses KV stale-while-revalidate under key repos:list:v2 — fresh under 5 minutes is served as-is, stale data is served immediately with a background refresh, and a KV TTL of 1 hour bounds staleness; SCM listing is enriched with a D1 RepoMetadataStore batch and every KV failure degrades rather than failing the request.

On the cold (no-cache) path the refresh promise is also registered with waitUntil while the response awaits the same run, because an early client abort would otherwise cancel the Worker before the KV write and leave a miss that can never self-heal — the stale-while-revalidate branch requires an entry to exist.

GitHub App installation tokens are cached in the same REPOS_CACHE KV namespace under github:installation-token:v1:<appId>:<installationId> with TTL min(remaining lifetime, 50 minutes) clamped to at least 1 second, and a cached token is only used if younger than 50 minutes with 5+ minutes remaining; KV errors are non-fatal in both directions.

KV is consumed through the shared CacheStore abstraction (get/put/delete with optional expirationTtl) built by createKvCacheStore, used by the control plane over REPOS_CACHE and by the bot workers over their own namespaces (SLACK_KV, GITHUB_KV, LINEAR_KV).

The KV namespace bound as REPOS_CACHE is still provisioned under the name open-inspect-session-index-* even though the session index and repo metadata were migrated from KV to D1 for queryability, so the binding is cache-only and never holds session state.

The control plane's data bindings are SESSION (Durable Object, class SessionDO), DB (D1), REPOS_CACHE (KV), MEDIA_BUCKET (R2), the optional IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_QUEUE (+ DLQ), and read-only AUTOFIX_QUEUE/AUTOFIX_DLQ metrics bindings.

packages/control-plane/wrangler.jsonc is a test-only configuration (production bindings come from Terraform), and it pins the DO migration { tag: 'v1', new_sqlite_classes: ['SessionDO'] } used by the Miniflare integration pool.

D1 migrations are applied by scripts/d1-migrate.sh, which validates filenames (numeric prefix required, no duplicate prefixes), tracks _schema_migrations by version AND exact filename so a reused version in another installation errors instead of skipping, and submits each migration with its ledger row as one SQL file so D1's atomic execution means a committed migration always has its row.
Terraform applies D1 migrations from null_resource.d1_migrations keyed by a SHA-256 over every migration file, and the control-plane Worker depends on it so schema precedes deployment.

Integration tests run the same migration set: vitest.integration.config.ts reads terraform/d1/migrations via readD1Migrations, passes them as TEST_MIGRATIONS, and setup applies them with applyD1Migrations against the wrangler.jsonc bindings at production's compatibility date.

Per-session Durable Object databases migrate themselves on activation: initSchema runs SCHEMA_SQL, then applyMigrations against its own _schema_migrations(id, applied_at) ledger, then INDEXES_SQL last so indexes may reference columns legacy tables lacked; string migrations swallow only duplicate-column/already-exists errors and function migrations must be idempotent because they may re-run after a crash.

schema.test.ts pins the DO migration contract: all migrations run on a fresh DO, recorded ids are skipped, malformed PRAGMA column metadata aborts without recording the migration id, and non-duplicate-column errors from string migrations are rethrown.

DO tables that also need a migration (session_repositories, attachments) are defined once as a shared SQL const referenced by both SCHEMA_SQL and the numbered migration, so the fresh-install and upgrade paths cannot diverge.

D1's 100-bound-parameter ceiling is an explicit store constraint: MAX_D1_QUERY_PARAMETERS drives bulkInsertStatements' floor(100/columnCount) row packing, IN-lists such as image-build scope reads chunk at 50, and unchunked queries fail outright rather than degrade.

D1 index shape is load-bearing: migration 0024 replaced a composite status IN (...) index with bare-equality partials after the recovery sweeps full-scanned the append-only automation_runs table and timed out, and later indexes (api_tokens.expires_at, image-build cleanup/recovery partials) follow the same discipline.

Because SQLite cannot add constraints, tightening a D1 contract is a create-new-table/copy/drop/rename migration — and 0059's copy is deliberately unfiltered so a malformed row aborts on the NOT NULL constraint before the old table is dropped, preserving data for explicit repair instead of silently deleting it.

A failed D1 projection is logged and swallowed rather than failing the session transition, so the index can drift; convergence comes from the abandoned-draft sweep's not_draft/repairStatus path and the next settled-turn updateMetrics, which is why 'anything scanning on status' can observe a stale row.

Inbox read state is a D1 projection rather than message history: sessions carry the latest terminal message triple (CHECK-constrained to be all-null or all-present) and session_read_states stores per-user last-read ids, so unread is computed in SQL without touching the Durable Object.

For pull requests the authority moved to D1: session_pull_requests is declared the authority record (keyed by the DO artifact id, monotonic provider_updated_at guard, plus a legacy identity unique index for rows without a repository external id) and the session DO's pr artifact is a live-view mirror.

A session's model-provider authentication is snapshotted into D1 at creation (session_model_provider_auth, one row per subscription provider, written in the same atomic batch as the session row) rather than stored in the Durable Object, and the DO reads it back through the index at spawn time.

Image-build status reads project an explicit public-safe column set rather than SELECT *, with a compile-time exhaustiveness check, so internal columns (callback token hash, provider session/image ids, lease state) can never reach a client.

An automation fans out over both its live repository selection and its environment selection, one child run per target, and each run snapshots its target at firing time so editing the selection never rewrites history or changes an in-flight launch.

The Worker's single queue entrypoint routes by queue name: batches from a queue starting with 'open-inspect-github-autofix-' go to the autofix handler, and everything else is consumed as image-build finalization jobs.

The Session Durable Object holds the D1 handle as a nullable field distinct from its embedded SQLite (this.sql), so session-local behaviour still works while index-dependent stores are constructed only when db is present.
